Buzz pollination or sonication is a technique used by some bees, such as solitary bees and bumblebees , to release pollen which is more or less firmly held by the anthers . [ 1 ] [ 2 ] The anthers of buzz-pollinated plant species are typically tubular, with an opening at only one end, and the pollen inside is smooth-grained and firmly attached. With self-fertile plants such as tomatoes, wind may be sufficient to shake loose the pollen through pores in the anther and accomplish pollination . Visits by bees may also shake loose some pollen, but more efficient pollination of those plants is accomplished by a few insect species who specialize in sonication or buzz pollination. [ 3 ] [ 4 ]
